chapters.label: Conversion and Proof
chapters.description: Start here for sane landing pages: proof, comparison, metrics, pricing, objections, and direct conversion scaffolding.

chapters.label: Enterprise Buying
chapters.description: Use this chapter when the page has to survive procurement, security review, rollout friction, and buyer-committee scrutiny.

chapters.label: Adoption and Operations
chapters.description: Pull from this chapter for onboarding, enablement, QBR, renewal, account planning, change management, and operating rhythm.

chapters.label: Narrative Systems
chapters.description: This is the bridge from ordinary SaaS sections into operating-model, storyline, topology, and executive-systems language.

chapters.label: Runtime Frontier
chapters.description: Treat this as a specialized layer. It is powerful, but it should be used intentionally after the page already has clear business structure.

chapters.label: Ritual Finale
chapters.description: These are the sharpest page-scale surfaces: command rooms, archives, bridges, cartography, councils, dossiers, ceremony, and boardroom systems.

starterKits.label: Fast Proof Page
starterKits.useWhen: You need a credible first-pass landing page without drifting into ornamental systems language.
starterKits.caution: Keep this lean. Six to eight sections is enough for a first useful composition.

starterKits.label: Enterprise Deal Room
starterKits.useWhen: You need one page that can support procurement, security, technical validation, and executive review at the same time.
starterKits.caution: Do not ship every enterprise block. Pick the pressure points that actually block the deal.

starterKits.label: Adoption and Expansion Loop
starterKits.useWhen: You need a customer-facing or internal success narrative that connects onboarding, adoption, renewal, and expansion.
starterKits.caution: Resist adding buyer-stage sections here. This kit should feel post-sale and operational.

starterKits.label: Operating System Page
starterKits.useWhen: You want the product to read like an operating model, not just a feature list.
starterKits.caution: Use one governing metaphor. Mixing too many system metaphors makes the page feel self-impressed.

starterKits.label: Boardroom Finale
starterKits.useWhen: You need a high-conviction executive page and you are willing to be selective and disciplined with theatrical surfaces.
starterKits.caution: This is the sharpest aesthetic layer. Use it only after the underlying buying story is already clear.
